title: Grammar: Formal Prepositional Phrases for Academic Analysis
grammarTip:
Формальные предложные фразы в академическом и деловом письме:

ВМЕСТО → ФОРМАЛЬНО:
because of → owing to / due to / as a result of
about → with regard to / concerning / in relation to
before → prior to / in advance of
after → following / subsequent to
despite → in spite of / notwithstanding
for → in favour of / in support of

ВВОД ТЕМЫ:
With reference to... · Regarding... · In terms of...
As far as X is concerned... · With respect to...

ЗАКЛЮЧЕНИЕ:
In conclusion / To sum up / Overall / To summarise
In light of the evidence / Taking everything into account

grammarTable.subject: in terms of
grammarTable.example: "In terms of communication style, high-context cultures differ significantly from low-context ones."

grammarTable.subject: with regard to
grammarTable.example: "With regard to linguistic diversity, the World Englishes framework is the most useful model."

grammarTable.subject: in relation to
grammarTable.short: in connection with / in respect of
grammarTable.example: "In relation to global communication, intelligibility matters more than accent."

grammarTable.subject: from the perspective of
grammarTable.example: "From the perspective of a language learner, this shift has significant implications."

grammarTable.subject: in the context of
grammarTable.example: "In the context of ELF, native-speaker norms are not the primary reference point."

grammarTable.subject: as far as X is concerned
grammarTable.short: when it comes to X / in X's case
grammarTable.example: "As far as language learners are concerned, intelligibility is the key measure of success."

grammarExtra.title: In Terms Of: Framing the Discussion

rows.form: "In terms of X" = from the standpoint of X / with respect to X
rows.example: "In terms of vocabulary, British and American English differ in many respects."

rows.form: Used to introduce the dimension of comparison or analysis
rows.example: "In terms of intelligibility, accent matters less than grammar and vocabulary."

rows.form: Common in academic, business, and analytical writing
rows.example: "In terms of global reach, English is unrivalled as a lingua franca."

rows.form: Can be followed by a noun, pronoun, or gerund
rows.example: "In terms of communicating effectively / communication effectiveness / this policy"

grammarExtra.title: With Regard To / With Reference To: Formal Reference

rows.form: "With regard to" = in respect of, concerning (formal)
rows.example: "With regard to language policy, there are no easy answers."

rows.form: "With reference to" = referring specifically to, in connection with
rows.example: "With reference to the research cited above, we can observe three key patterns."

rows.form: Both are more formal than "about" or "regarding"
rows.example: "With regard to this issue" = more formal than "about this issue"

rows.form: Often used in business correspondence and academic writing
rows.example: "With reference to your request of 12th March, we are pleased to confirm…"

grammarExtra.title: From the Perspective Of / From a X Perspective: Analytical Framing

rows.form: "From the perspective of X" = as seen by X / through X's lens
rows.example: "From the perspective of a multilingual learner, the native speaker model is limiting."

rows.form: "From a X perspective" = taking X as the analytical framework
rows.example: "From a sociolinguistic perspective, code-switching is a sophisticated communicative practice."

rows.form: "From X's perspective" = as X would see it
rows.example: "From Kachru's perspective, all World Englishes are equally legitimate."

rows.form: Useful for presenting one analytical view among several
rows.example: "From a consequentialist perspective… From a deontological perspective…"

grammarExtra.title: As Far As X Is Concerned: Limiting the Domain

rows.form: "As far as X is concerned" = when it comes to X / in X's case
rows.example: "As far as language learners are concerned, communicative effectiveness is the key goal."

rows.form: X can be a noun, pronoun, or noun phrase
rows.example: "As far as ELF is concerned / as far as this study is concerned"

rows.form: Equivalent to "in terms of X" but more personal in tone
rows.example: "As far as I am concerned, the policy is the wrong approach." (= in my view)

rows.form: Also used to limit scope: "as far as we know / as far as possible"
rows.example: "As far as we know, this is the first study of its kind in this region."

grammarExtra.title: Common Errors with Formal Prepositional Phrases

rows.form: ❌ In terms of I prefer British English.
rows.example: ✅ In terms of accent, I prefer British English. ("in terms of" + noun, not subject)

rows.form: ❌ With regard of language policy…
rows.example: ✅ With regard to language policy… ("with regard TO" not "with regard OF")

rows.form: ❌ From the perspective of that…
rows.example: ✅ From the perspective of the learner, that… ("from the perspective of + noun")

rows.form: ❌ As far as concerned, the research shows…
rows.example: ✅ As far as language learners are concerned, the research shows… (need the subject)

Which sentence uses a formal prepositional phrase correctly?
opts: "In terms of I think English is important."
"From the perspective of multilingualism, diversity is a strength."
"With regard of accent, I prefer British English."
"As far concerned, the study is complete."
questions.correct: "From the perspective of multilingualism, diversity is a strength."
questions.hint: "From the perspective of + noun" — correct structure
